citation: Buysse, V., Castro, D. C., & Peisner-Feinberg, E. (2010). Effects of a professional development program on classroom practices and outcomes for Latino dual language learners. Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 25(2), 194-206. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecresq.2009.10.001
design: RCT (cluster-randomized); assignment level = Teacher/Class. 55 lead pre-K teachers (26 intervention, 29 control) randomized to Nuestros Ninos language/literacy PD vs business-as-usual; 193 Latino Spanish-English dual language learners (92 intervention, 101 control), ~4 children/classroom. Subject = early language & literacy (assessed in both English and Spanish). Grade = Pre-K. North Carolina More at Four Pre-Kindergarten Program. Goal-2 development study, one school year.
problems: Paper reports Cohen's d (Table 4) but NOT a model-based SE for the standardized effect; Table 5 mixed-model parameter estimates (b/SE) are in raw score units, not standardized, so they cannot be directly converted to g without each measure's SD (provided only as raw posttest SDs, not difference-score SDs). g was therefore computed from the reported d via g=J*d, and g_var via the naive student-level approximation. The d point estimate IS classroom/pretest-adjusted (mixed model on fall->spring difference scores), so g itself accounts for clustering; only g_var lacks a cluster correction (ICC not reported, n_clusters=55). All 16 outcomes are early language/literacy and mapped to Reading per the task instruction (language/literacy->Reading; no STEM/math outcomes exist in this study). The PAT phonological-awareness measures are researcher-made with LOW internal consistency (Cronbach alpha .52 English / .59 Spanish overall; subscales .19-.42), a limitation the authors flag. Only 2 of 16 child contrasts were statistically significant (Spanish PAT Total g=+0.69 & its Rhyme-Matching subscale g=+0.68; English PAT Onset-Segmentation-&-Matching subscale g=+0.61); all other contrasts ns. The meta-analysis included only independent/standardized measures, so the standardized_independent outcomes (WLPB-R, PPVT-III, TVIP) are most likely the ones used centrally.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Nuestros Ninos PD vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Woodcock Language Proficiency Battery-Revised (WLPB-R), Spanish form - Broad Language
effect_sizes.timepoint: spring (end of school year, post; Spanish assessment)
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*d, J=0.9961 (df=N-2=191); d = author-reported Cohen's d (Table 4) computed as adjusted intervention-vs-control difference in fall->spring LS-mean difference scores (mixed model adjusting for classroom, %Latino, teacher education, gender, age). Standardizing SD = pooled SD of difference scores implied by author's Cohen's d. g_var = J^2*[(n_t+n_c)/(n_t*n_c) + d^2/(2*(n_t+n_c))] (naive student-level approx; model SE for standardized d not reported).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.201 Table 4 (effect sizes/means); p.202-203 Table 5 (mixed-model parameter estimates)
effect_sizes.notes: Spanish oral language proficiency; ns (study condition b=2.47, SE=1.71, p=.16, Table 5). Spanish-language assessment. Point estimate (d) is from a classroom-adjusted mixed model so g itself accounts for clustering; only g_var is a student-level approximation needing central cluster-correction (ICC not reported). Pretest-adjusted via fall->spring difference scores.
